cards.explanation: The answer is that they had no opportunity to show it. Paul says they were indeed concerned, but they had no opportunity to show it (Philippians 4:10). Caring and getting the chance to act on it are two different things, friends. I've had a whole batch of good intentions sitting in my head with no oven in sight.

The word is content. Paul says he has learned to be content regardless of his circumstances (Philippians 4:11). Notice the word "learned." He didn't wake up with it, friends. I'm still learning it myself, especially when a fresh batch is cooling right next to me.

The answer is False. The secret isn't about always having plenty. Paul says he has learned "…the secret of being filled and being hungry, of having plenty and having need." (Philippians 4:12). He knows both sides of the counter, friends. That's what makes his secret worth listening to.

The answer is through Christ who gives him strength. Paul says, "I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength." (Philippians 4:13). The strength comes from Christ, and Paul says so plainly. It's right there in the verse, no gym wall needed.

The word is affliction. Paul says, "…you have done well to share in my affliction." (Philippians 4:14). They stepped into his hard season with him. I think that's the kind of friend who shows up when the oven's broken, not just when the cookies are done.

The answer is none. Paul says when he left Macedonia, "…no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving." (Philippians 4:15). Only the Philippians. Zero other churches, friends. That's a short list with one name on it.

The answer is again and again. Paul says that even in Thessalonica, "…you provided for my needs again and again." (Philippians 4:16). Not a one-time gift, friends. They kept showing up, like someone who comes back to the bakery every single week.

The answer is False. Paul says, "Not that I am seeking a gift, but I am looking for the fruit that may be credited to your account." (Philippians 4:17). He's not fishing for presents, friends. He's looking at what their giving grows.

The answer is True. Paul says, "I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus." (Philippians 4:18). The gifts came to him through Epaphroditus, friends. Paul's cup was full and then some.

The answer is a fragrant offering. Paul says the gifts are "…a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God." (Philippians 4:18). Gifts given to Paul became something pleasing to God. Your kindness is never small to Him, friends.

The answer is His glorious riches in Christ Jesus. Paul writes, "And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus." (Philippians 4:19). The measure is God's riches, not our pockets. That's a cookie jar with no bottom, friends.

The answer is those from Caesar's household. Paul says, "All the saints send you greetings, especially those from the household of Caesar." (Philippians 4:22). Caesar was the Roman emperor. Saints from his household are sending hello to Philippi, friends.
